title: fix(runtime,plugin-auth)!: a banned user's OAuth access tokens and refresh grants are refused while the ban holds
body:
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here

> **Base is `main`.** The pull request this branch was stacked on (#30287) has landed on `main` as `f4cd4ec879`. This branch merged `origin/main` at `f6faf75116` in `949fd3f1e4` (a merge, no rebase); the files both sides added are `main`'s copies, so the diff against `main` is this change alone.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：用户被封禁期间，其 OAuth 访问令牌在 MCP 入口按"无法验证的令牌"拒绝，在 `/oauth2/userinfo` 按无效令牌应答、在 `/oauth2/introspect` 按非活动令牌应答；令牌端点不再为其签发新令牌（refresh 与授权码兑换均被拒）。封禁确认框与管理员、认证文档同步写明。
- 为什么改：封禁已拒绝该用户的登录、会话与 API key；OAuth 令牌及其续期是同一用户的凭据，在读取或签发它们的入口适用同一规则。
- 风险与回滚：MCP 入口每个 OAuth 凭据多一次按主键读 sys_user 封禁列（读失败 503）；introspection 每个活动应答多一次读用户行（读失败则请求失败，不臆造应答）；令牌端点与 userinfo 不增加读取。不吊销、不改写任何令牌行；授权码在封禁期间被出示即作废，客户端需重新登录。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.ts（userinfo 与 introspection 两处拒绝）；packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts（令牌端点，授权码分支的先后顺序见文件头）；packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts（MCP 入口读取与 503 分类）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts`，预期全部通过（真实 provider 上：封禁用户的 refresh、授权码、userinfo、introspection 应答与无效凭据一致，解封或到期后恢复）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

While a user's ban holds, the rule holds at these doors, and only these:

- **MCP door.** An OAuth access token whose subject is banned resolves as a token that does not verify: no principal, no fall-back to a cookie session, the same `401` body and `WWW-Authenticate` header. An agent forward credential acting for a banned user resolves as one that does not redeem. The ban is read where the credential becomes its user (`resolveExecutionContext` → `isOAuthSubjectBanned`, `packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts`), with the shared predicate `isUserBanInForce` from `@objectstack/core`. The verifier (`verifyMcpAccessToken`) stays the local, I/O-free signature check.
- **Token endpoint.** The provider mints a banned user no token. A `refresh_token` grant is answered as an invalid refresh token (`400 invalid_grant`, `invalid refresh token`) and writes nothing. An `authorization_code` exchange is refused and the code is spent: when the ban ended the user's sessions, as the ban routes do, the provider's own session answer refuses it (`400 invalid_request`); otherwise it is answered as an invalid code (`400 invalid_grant`, `invalid code`). Any extension grant that issues through the provider is refused as an invalid grant. The refusal runs in the provider's callback `customTokenResponseFields`, which receives the user row the provider already read (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts`; its header records the order on each grant and why this hook).
- **Userinfo.** `/oauth2/userinfo` answers a banned user's access token as an access token that does not verify (`401 invalid_token`, the provider's description and `WWW-Authenticate` challenge), the answer a made-up token gets. It runs in `customUserInfoClaims`, on the user row the provider already read, before the locale claim (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.ts`).
- **Introspection.** `/oauth2/introspect` answers a banned user's access and refresh tokens as inactive (`{ "active": false }`), the answer a made-up, expired or revoked token gets (RFC 7662 §2.2). It runs as a section of AuthManager's global after-hook, on the provider's active answer, with one read of the subject's user row through the provider's adapter (same file).
- **Expiry.** A ban with an expiry stops binding once it has passed, exactly as sign-in reads it, at every door above.
- **Not a revocation.** No token, refresh token or consent row is revoked or rewritten; lifting the ban (or its expiry) admits the same access token at the MCP door and lets the same refresh token renew.
- **Cost.** One primary-key read of `sys_user` (`id`, `banned`, `ban_expires`), as the system, per OAuth credential the MCP door resolves; one user-row read per active introspection answer that names a user; zero at the token and userinfo endpoints. A store fault on the MCP door's read is `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` naming `sys_user`; a store fault on the introspection read fails the request (`500`) rather than answering active or inactive; a missing user row or an unprovisioned table keeps today's answer.
- **The words.** The Ban User confirmation (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`, its AI description and the three translated bundles), `content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx` (lifecycle actions and the offboarding row) and `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` (the `ban-user` route) name OAuth access tokens and token refreshes among what a ban refuses. `@objectstack/platform-objects` joins the changeset at patch.
- The `plugin-auth` APIError code pin now also reads an OAuth 2.0 error response (a literal `error` beside an `error_description`, RFC 6749 §5.2) as a coded body, with fixtures for both directions: the token-endpoint refusal must answer exactly as the provider's own error does, which carries no ADR-0112 `code`.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.test.ts` — new top-level describe: banned subject resolves exactly as an unverified bearer; a future expiry binds, a passed one does not; not-banned, unbanned, no-row and no-table controls admit as before; a ban read that throws is `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` naming `sys_user`; cost pinned at one ban-column read per token and none for an unverified bearer; a forward credential for a banned user resolves as one that does not redeem.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.test.ts` — the refusal against the provider's own error (class, status, body, headers) for each grant type; expiry in both spellings; not-banned and no-user controls.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.test.ts` (new) — the userinfo refusal (status, body, challenge; expiry in both spellings; controls); the introspection section (rewritten in place for a banned subject; expiry; not-banned and no-row controls; inactive, subject-less, other-path and non-object answers read nothing; a read that throws fails and leaves the answer as produced; the provider's adapter is the default reader; AuthManager's global after-hook runs the section).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts` — on the real provider with AuthManager's own options: a banned user's refresh grant equals an invalid refresh token's answer and writes no refresh row, and renews once the ban lapses; a code issued before a ban that ended the user's sessions gets the provider's session answer, starts no refresh family and is spent; a code exchanged while the user's session survived equals a code never issued and starts no refresh family; userinfo for a banned user's token equals a made-up token's answer and reads the claims again once the ban lapses; introspection of a banned user's access and refresh tokens equals a made-up token's answer and is active again once the ban lapses; not-banned controls for each.
- `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/action-confirm-one-dialog.test.ts` — the Ban User confirmation pinned word for word, now naming OAuth access tokens and token refreshes.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts` — booted showcase, real DCR → authorize → consent → token: `initialize`, `query_records`, `create_record` and the refresh grant against a made-up token / an invalid refresh token, the refused write landing nothing; peer, unban and timed-ban controls. Its header declares its measured test budget (20 s: 13.13 s of tests, the slower of two local runs, × 1.25, rounded up).

## Acceptance notes

- The `plugin-auth` APIError code pin gains a third accepted shape, the RFC 6749 §5.2 error response, so a token-endpoint refusal can carry exactly the provider's own body; a literal `error` with no `error_description`, or a non-literal `error`, is still reported (fixtures in both directions).
- An authorization code presented for a banned user is spent whichever refusal answers it, as the provider consumes a code before it reads the code's session; after the ban the client signs the user in again.
- The banned-subject dogfood file's 20 s test budget is a local reading on a shared box; no CI reading exists yet, so it should be re-measured on CI.

## Verification

Readings at head `942ee6846660` unless stated. Readings marked `11504e470d` were taken one commit earlier; `942ee68466` adds only the budget header line of `oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts`. `packages/runtime` is unchanged since `949fd3f1e4`, so its reading from that head stands.
